stopOnEntry.description: Stop on the program's first line.

commands.title: Add to Cursor / Windsurf MCP Config

walkthroughs.title: Get started with craftos-mcp
walkthroughs.description: Run ComputerCraft Lua without Minecraft, test it, and hand the emulator to your AI agent.

steps.title: Run a program
steps.description:
Open any .lua file and run it in the emulator, beside your code. The first run downloads the engine and builds the CC:Tweaked ROM (about a minute, once).
[Run in CraftOS](command:craftos-mcp.runInCraftOS)

steps.title: Give it a world
steps.description:
A name.world.json next to name.lua adds monitors, players, chests and modded blocks around the computer. It opens in the World Editor.
[New World for This File](command:craftos-mcp.newWorld)

steps.title: Write a test
steps.description:
Files named name.test.lua show in the Testing view, with Run test above each test; a failure points at the line Lua named.
[New Test for This File](command:craftos-mcp.newTest)

steps.title: Debug it
steps.description:
Click left of a line number for a breakpoint and press F5 on a .lua file. The program stops there, and you can step and look at its variables.
[Debug in CraftOS](command:craftos-mcp.debugInCraftOS)

steps.title: Get autocomplete
steps.description:
With the Lua extension (sumneko.lua), fs, term, peripheral and the mod peripherals complete and show their docs, and typos get underlined.
[Set Up Lua Types](command:craftos-mcp.setUpLuaTypes)

steps.title: Let your agent use it
steps.description:
In VS Code the agent already has the craftos tools. For Claude Code, Cursor or Windsurf, add the server to their config.
[Add to Claude Code](command:craftos-mcp.addToClaudeCode)
[Add to Cursor / Windsurf](command:craftos-mcp.addToEditor)

steps.title: Match your pack
steps.description:
Pick the Minecraft version and the mods your pack has, from here or the CraftOS item in the status bar. In a big repo, set the folder the computers see.
[Pick Minecraft Version](command:craftos-mcp.pickMinecraftVersion)
[Pick Addons](command:craftos-mcp.pickAddons)
[Open Settings](command:craftos-mcp.openSettings)

enumDescriptions: CC:Tweaked 1.101.3, the most complete simulation of the mods
craftos-mcp.minecraftVersion.markdownDescription: The Minecraft version computers start on (`CRAFTOS_VERSION`). **craftos-mcp: Pick Minecraft Version** and the status bar item set this for the workspace. A world file's own `version` still wins.

craftos-mcp.addons.markdownDescription: Mods to simulate besides CC:Tweaked (`CRAFTOS_ADDONS`): `all`, `none`, or ids separated by commas, such as `create,mekanism`. Empty means every addon the Minecraft version has. **craftos-mcp: Pick Addons** gives you a checklist and writes this for the workspace; the ids are in [the addon list](https://github.com/Akkiruk/craftos-mcp#choose-your-mods). A world file's own `addons` still wins.

craftos-mcp.workspace.markdownDescription: The folder the computers see as their files, relative to the workspace folder, such as `workspace` or `src/lua` (`CRAFTOS_WORKSPACE`). Empty means the workspace folder itself for the MCP server and the tests, and the program's own folder for **Run in CraftOS**. Set it in a big repo: the emulator copies this folder into every computer it starts.

craftos-mcp.rerunOnSave.markdownDescription: While a **Run in CraftOS** panel is open, saving its program, another `.lua` file in the folder it runs in, or its `.world.json` runs the program over in the panel. A program being debugged is left alone.

craftos-mcp.testCodeLens.markdownDescription: Show **Run test** and **Debug test** above each `ccunit.test` in `*.test.lua` files.

craftos-mcp.diagnostics.markdownDescription: Warn in `.lua` files about what the computer's Minecraft version or pack lacks: `goto` and labels on 1.18.2 (Lua 5.1), CraftOS-PC's own APIs, `os.shutdown` with an exit code (emulator-only), and peripherals of an addon that is switched off. Each warning has a quick fix. A world file's `version` and `addons` count for the program next to it; otherwise `#craftos-mcp.minecraftVersion#` and `#craftos-mcp.addons#` do.

craftos-mcp.testTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a `*.test.lua` file may run in the Testing view before it counts as timed out.

enumDescriptions: Ask once in each ComputerCraft workspace before adding the types
Add them to every ComputerCraft workspace without asking
Leave workspaces alone (Set Up Lua Types still works)
craftos-mcp.luaTypes.markdownDescription: CC:Tweaked types for the Lua extension (`sumneko.lua`): autocomplete and hover docs for `fs`, `term`, `peripheral`, the mod peripherals and `ccunit`. They go into the workspace's `Lua.workspace.library`, added to what's there; `Lua.runtime.version` and `Lua.runtime.builtin` are only set where you haven't set them. **craftos-mcp: Remove Lua Types** takes them out again.

enumDescriptions: Register it in workspaces that look like ComputerCraft projects (Lua files, *.world.json, craftos.json, the CC:Tweaked Lua types in the settings), unless the workspace's .vscode/mcp.json already has a server with craftos in its name, command or args
Register it in every workspace, ComputerCraft or not, unless .vscode/mcp.json already has a craftos server
Always register it, in every workspace and even next to a craftos server in .vscode/mcp.json (the agent sees both tool sets)
craftos-mcp.registerServer.markdownDescription: Whether the extension gives VS Code its own craftos-mcp MCP server, and where. By default (`auto`) only in workspaces that look like ComputerCraft projects, so the agent in your other projects doesn't carry the emulator's tools; `everywhere` turns it on in all of them. **Run in CraftOS**, the debugger and the Testing view work either way.

craftos-mcp.command.markdownDescription: For working on craftos-mcp itself: how to start it, as a command and its arguments, without the subcommand. Empty (the default) means `npx -y craftos-mcp@<the version this extension was built for>`, and most people should leave it so. For a clone: `["node", "/path/to/craftos-mcp/apps/cli/dist/index.js"]`.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm run build
